name: dependabot-lock-automation
title: Automate requirements-dev.lock regeneration for Dependabot PRs
description: Make a Dependabot pip PR reach green without a maintainer running `make lock`, so the sd-update-deps auto-merge class stops being structurally empty for this repository. Dependabot bumps requirements-dev.txt only, but nothing installs from that file, so check-dev-requirements-lock.py fails every bot PR on pin-mismatch. The gating design question is the credential model: Dependabot-triggered workflows get a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN, so pushing a regenerated lock back to a bot branch needs an elevated credential in a job that runs `make lock` over bot-branch content. design.md must settle trigger, write scope, checkout ref, and escalation containment before implementation starts.
creator: sdelmas
notes: WON'T-DO, not implemented. Resolved by deciding against CI automation: the push cannot use GITHUB_TOKEN (GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events it generates, so the relocked head would never re-run tests), which forces a GitHub App token and a standing contents:write credential reachable from pull_request_target to save ~2-3 hours a year. Shipped `make relock-pr PR=<n>` instead. Trellis has no cancelled status; 'completed' here means the task reached a decision, NOT that the automation was built. Accepted consequence: the sd-update-deps pip auto-merge class stays empty. See design.md DECISION section.
